reports.title: Campaign categories: revenue per send

items.lab: BLOG revenue per send, the highest of any category
SEGMENT revenue per send, the lowest

blocks.html: Since 23 June 2026 the cadence has run four kinds of campaign: SEGMENT (new, targeted to specific audiences), BLOG, LATCH & FLOW, and the broad GENERAL sends. This report looks at how each category performs on the number that matters when billing is per email: revenue per send.

blocks.cap: 23 Jun to 27 Aug 2026. Klaviyo-attributed revenue, email only. Each bar is the average revenue earned per campaign in that category.
blocks.title: Average revenue per send, by category

blocks.html: You pay per email, so the figure that justifies each send is the revenue it brings in. On that measure BLOG leads at about $3,888 a send, just ahead of the broad GENERAL sends at about $3,662. SEGMENT trails at about $854 a send. That is not a creative problem, it is an audience-size one: SEGMENT goes to much smaller, targeted lists, roughly 29,000 recipients versus about 160,000 for a broad send.

blocks.cap: Total Klaviyo-attributed revenue across every campaign in each category, 23 Jun to 27 Aug 2026.
blocks.title: Total revenue in the window, by category

blocks.html: Across the window BLOG earned about $46.7k from 12 sends while SEGMENT earned about $8.5k from 10 sends. SEGMENT does win on efficiency, roughly $0.029 of revenue per recipient against $0.024 for BLOG and $0.022 for GENERAL, but that is a secondary metric here. Because billing is per email, a category that wins on revenue per recipient yet lags on revenue per send costs more for less total return.
Can we send more without shrinking the list? If extra campaigns pushed people to unsubscribe, we would expect the subscriber base to stall or fall as volume rose. It does the opposite.

blocks.cap: Bars: campaigns sent that week, all categories. Line: cumulative net new email subscribers (subscribes minus unsubscribes). 23 Jun to 24 Aug 2026, nine complete weeks.
blocks.title: Campaign volume vs the subscriber base

blocks.html: Across the nine weeks the list grew by a net 24,346 subscribers while we sent 47 campaigns, and it gained subscribers every single week. The clearest signal is the week of 28 July: our heaviest week at 8 campaigns still added +3,858 net subscribers, among the best weeks in the window. Unsubscribes stayed roughly flat, about 1,400 to 2,300 a week, regardless of how much we sent. More sending is not costing us the list.

Recommendation. There is headroom to push a little harder. Lean into more BLOG campaigns, the category returning the most per send, and test broader sends to the fuller list. We will trial that heavier mix for one to two months and watch the subscriber base closely. If growth holds, as it has here, we know we were leaving revenue on the table and can keep the higher cadence. If it starts to eat into the list, we ease back. Either way we will circle back on the results.

reports.summary: BLOG campaigns return the most revenue per send. SEGMENT wins on revenue per recipient but trails on total, so it costs more for less overall return. And more sending has not shrunk the list, so there is room to push harder.
